thesis: NEW IDEA, conditional. XLE is the only sector leader that has actually pulled back rather than sitting on its highs, which is why it is the only one whose arithmetic clears the floors today. It fell 13.2% from 70.151 to 59.55 in November and is now resting on a RISING 200-day at 59.84, which it has tested and held on three consecutive sessions (lows 59.745, 59.552, 59.630) before closing back up at 60.90. Energy is also structurally the right asset for the confirmed regime — the Fed is hiking because inflation is accelerating, and energy is a nominal-price-linked real asset rather than a multiple that compresses.
key_risk: The OPEC+ ministerial on 2026-11-29 is a binary supply event two days away and it is the reason to wait rather than buy. If the group restores a tranche of 2022-halted output for 2027, crude and energy equities gap down through the 200-day on Monday's open and the 57.20 stop is of no use against a weekend gap — that is precisely why the entry is conditional on the outcome instead of placed ahead of it. The secondary risk is that a hiking Fed into a slowdown destroys oil DEMAND, which would make the November breakdown the start of a trend rather than a pullback.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that November's 15% decline is the market correctly front-running an OPEC+ supply increase, making the 200-day a shelf that is about to break rather than support. There is real evidence on the other side: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq are all currently producing WELL BELOW their existing quotas because Strait of Hormuz constraints persist, so a higher quota need not deliver higher actual barrels — the group has been raising paper targets into a market that cannot physically fill them. That is why the trade is worth preparing for rather than abandoning. It does not refute the risk, which is why the recommendation is to wait for the answer rather than to pre-position on it.
